topline.text: The one genuinely new story in the last 24-48 hours: ONS figures published yesterday show NEET numbers easing on the quarter but still up on the year - and it's young women driving that annual rise, worth flagging for transitions and post-16 work.

Otherwise a quiet 24-48 hours - no fresh DfE, Ofsted, SEND/AP, exclusions, safeguarding or funding stories broke, and nothing new from Sheffield or South Yorkshire either, so today's briefing is short rather than padded.

items.lede: NEET total dips on the quarter, but the annual trend is going the wrong way for young women
items.body: ONS estimates 959,000 16-24-year-olds in the UK were NEET in July-September 2026 - down 22,000 on the previous quarter, but up 17,000 on a year earlier. The breakdown: roughly 476,000 young women NEET (up ~41,000 on the year) against about 483,000 young men (down ~24,000). Youth Futures Foundation says the figures underline the need for sustained, evidence-based action rather than one-off interventions - relevant context for schools tracking post-16 destinations and early identification of pupils at risk of disengaging.

box.text: 16-24-year-olds in the UK classed as NEET in July-September 2026 - down 22,000 on the quarter, but up 17,000 on the year. Figures come from the Labour Force Survey, so the ONS flags normal sampling variability on sub-group breakdowns.
